canonical.title: BFF options in .NET 10: Duende.BFF, YARP, or hand-rolled

parent.title: Pure React 19 SPA or a .NET 10 BFF? A decision framework for an internal admin console

siblings.title: In-memory tokens vs cookie-backed BFF sessions under XSS: what each architecture actually buys you
siblings.summary: httpOnly cookies do not stop XSS — they convert silent token exfiltration into loud, tab-bound session riding.

siblings.title: Does the IETF browser-based-apps BCP apply to an internal admin console?
siblings.summary: The BCP names "business applications" in its strongest recommendation, so an internal console is in scope — but it is a trade-off, not a normative MUST.

siblings.title: Refresh tokens and silent renew in a browser SPA (2026)
siblings.summary: Iframe silent renew is dead cross-site but alive same-site; DPoP only really works on Keycloak.

siblings.title: Greenfield BFF vs retrofitting later: where the asymmetry actually is
siblings.summary: Adding a BFF later is a two-way door. The one-way door is the API, not the frontend.

siblings.title: What a BFF costs you every day: OpenAPI codegen and the local dev loop
siblings.summary: A path-preserving BFF leaves OpenAPI codegen essentially untouched; the daily cost is one extra process.

sources.title: https://duendesoftware.com/pricing
sources.claim: Duende 2026 list prices: Lite $5,750/yr, Standard $12,500/yr, Advanced $24,900/yr, each bundling a BFF front-end quota; add-ons priced separately.

sources.title: https://duendesoftware.com/products/communityedition
sources.claim: Community Edition eligibility is revenue-based: <$1M USD annual gross revenue and <$3M USD capital, or non-profit with <$1M budget; excludes redistribution and customer-facing deployments.

sources.title: https://wrapt.dev/blog/standalone-duende-bff-for-any-spa
sources.claim: A standalone Duende BFF for a React SPA against Keycloak is ~50 lines of Program.cs (AddBff().AddRemoteApis(), __Host- cookie, AddOpenIdConnect to Keycloak, MapRemoteBffApiEndpoint).

sources.title: https://github.com/DuendeSoftware/foss
sources.claim: Duende.AccessTokenManagement and the other Duende FOSS libraries are Apache-2.0 licensed and free.

sources.title: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/blazor/security/blazor-web-app-with-oidc?view=aspnetcore-10.0
sources.claim: Microsoft ships an official BFF-with-YARP + Aspire sample for .NET 10, using MapForwarder transforms to attach the access token and a custom CookieOidcRefresher for non-interactive refresh.

sources.title: https://github.com/oidcproxydotnet/OidcProxy.Net
sources.claim: OidcProxy.Net is an LGPL-3.0 open-source identity-aware reverse proxy built on YARP implementing the BFF/token-handler pattern; supports Keycloak, IdentityServer, Auth0, Entra ID and OpenIddict.

sources.title: https://github.com/oauth2-proxy/oauth2-proxy
sources.claim: oauth2-proxy is an MIT-licensed reverse proxy providing OIDC authentication for many providers; latest v7.15.3 (June 2026).

sources.title: https://nestenius.se/net/bff-in-asp-net-core-5-automatic-token-renewal/
sources.claim: Hand-rolled token renewal is discouraged: race conditions, multi-instance token storage conflicts, and real incidents of tokens leaking to the wrong users.

sources.title: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/breaking-changes/10/cookie-authentication-api-endpoints?view=aspnetcore-10.0
sources.claim: .NET 10 breaking change: cookie auth returns 401/403 for known API endpoints (IApiEndpointMetadata) instead of redirecting to login.

sources.title: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/8175
sources.claim: Built-in OAuth 2 refresh-token support in ASP.NET Core is still an open issue (opened 2019), now milestoned .NET 11 Planning.

sources.title: https://docs.duendesoftware.com/general/licensing/
sources.claim: Duende BFF is licensed as its own product (Starter/Enterprise editions), requires a licence for production, trial mode limits to five sessions per host (not technically enforced), validation is fully local, and small orgs are pointed at the community edition.

sources.title: https://docs.duendesoftware.com/bff/fundamentals/session/server-side-sessions/
sources.claim: Duende BFF server-side sessions (AddServerSideSessions, EF store) keep the cookie small and constant and allow revocation on back-channel logout.

sources.title: https://duendesoftware.com/blog/20250325-understanding-antiforgery-in-aspnetcore
sources.claim: Duende BFF's CSRF protection requires only an X-CSRF: 1 header, which forces a CORS preflight for cross-origin calls and thereby isolates callers to the same origin.

sources.title: https://www.nuget.org/packages/Duende.BFF
sources.claim: Duende.BFF latest is 4.2.0 (2026-06-10), targets .NET 10.0, 4.7M total downloads, depends on Duende.AccessTokenManagement.OpenIdConnect.

sources.title: https://github.com/DuendeSoftware/products
sources.claim: The DuendeSoftware/products repo hosts IdentityServer, BFF and the DPoP JWT-bearer extensions under Duende's proprietary licence.

sources.title: https://docs.duendesoftware.com/bff/upgrading/bff-v3-to-v4/
sources.claim: BFF v3 to v4 is a breaking upgrade: TokenType renamed to RequiredTokenType, RequireAccessToken() to WithAccessToken(), IUserService to IUserEndpoint, and a breaking DB schema change (UserSessions.ApplicationName to PartitionKey).

sources.title: https://api.nuget.org/v3/registration5-gz-semver2/duende.bff/index.json
sources.claim: Duende.BFF 4.1.2 (2026-03-13) targeted net8.0/net9.0/net10.0; 4.2.0 (2026-06-10) targets net10.0 only.

sources.title: https://github.com/dotnet/yarp
sources.claim: YARP is an MIT-licensed reverse-proxy toolkit from Microsoft, ~9.6k stars, latest 2.3.0; its README does not cover authentication.

sources.title: https://docs.duendesoftware.com/accesstokenmanagement/
sources.claim: Duende.AccessTokenManagement.OpenIdConnect gives automatic access-token lifetime management using the refresh token for calls on behalf of the logged-in user, and is Apache-2.0 open source.

sources.title: https://damienbod.com/2024/09/09/implement-openid-connect-back-channel-logout-using-asp-net-core-keycloak-and-net-aspire/
sources.claim: ASP.NET Core has no built-in OIDC back-channel logout: you implement the webhook, validate the logout token, persist to a distributed cache and check it on every request via a cookie event handler.

sources.title: https://www.nuget.org/packages/Yarp.ReverseProxy
sources.claim: Yarp.ReverseProxy latest stable is 2.3.0 (27 Feb 2025) with 68.7M total downloads; no newer preview exists.

sources.title: https://oauth2-proxy.github.io/oauth2-proxy/configuration/overview
sources.claim: oauth2-proxy can pass the access token as X-Forwarded-Access-Token (pass-access-token), the ID token as a Bearer Authorization header (pass-authorization-header), set-authorization-header only in nginx auth_request mode, supports cookie-refresh and a Redis session store.

sources.title: https://docs.duendesoftware.com/bff/architecture/
sources.claim: Duende BFF exposes /bff/user, /bff/login and /bff/logout, enforces an X-CSRF header on API routes, and keeps tokens on the server.

sources.title: https://docs.duendesoftware.com/bff/fundamentals/apis/remote/
sources.claim: Duende BFF's remote-API forwarder uses YARP internally (Duende.BFF.Yarp package) and maps remote APIs with MapRemoteBffApiEndpoint(...).WithAccessToken(RequiredTokenType.User), with automatic anti-forgery and token management.

sources.title: https://duendesoftware.com/blog/20251202-duende-bffv4-now-available-multi-frontend-opentelemetry-and-simplified-security
sources.claim: Duende BFF v4 shipped 2 December 2025 with multi-frontend hosting, OpenTelemetry and simplified automatic configuration.

sources.title: https://github.com/orgs/DuendeSoftware/discussions/557
sources.claim: Duende staff confirm the production licence key may be reused in dev/test/UAT; validation is local with no phoning home and no aggregation risk.

sources.title: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/servers/yarp/authn-authz?view=aspnetcore-10.0
sources.claim: YARP performs no authentication unless the app configures ASP.NET Core auth; with OIDC the result is an auth cookie that flows to the destination as a normal header, and swapping to a bearer token requires custom request transforms.

sources.title: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/servers/yarp/transforms?view=aspnetcore-10.0
sources.claim: YARP request transforms are added programmatically via AddTransforms/AddRequestTransform, which is the hook for injecting an Authorization header.

sources.title: https://github.com/dotnet/blazor-samples/blob/main/10.0/BlazorWebAppOidcBffAutoYarpAspire/BlazorWebAppOidc/Program.cs
sources.claim: Microsoft's .NET 10 BFF sample wires cookie+OIDC, uses MapForwarder with AddRequestTransform and GetTokenAsync("access_token") to attach the bearer token, calls AddHttpForwarderWithServiceDiscovery, and documents PAR as the default (PushedAuthorizationBehavior.UseIfAvailable).

sources.title: https://api.nuget.org/v3/registration5-gz-semver2/duende.accesstokenmanagement.openidconnect/index.json
sources.claim: Duende.AccessTokenManagement.OpenIdConnect 4.2.0 (2026-03-18) is Apache-2.0 and targets net8.0/net9.0/net10.0.

sources.title: https://timdeschryver.dev/blog/secure-your-yarp-bff-with-cookie-based-authentication
sources.claim: A YARP-based BFF needs hand-written /bff/login, /bff/logout and /bff/user endpoints on top of AddCookie + AddOpenIdConnect; the walkthrough does not cover antiforgery or refresh.

sources.title: https://timdeschryver.dev/blog/forwarding-authenticated-calls-to-a-downstream-api-using-yarp
sources.claim: Injecting the token into proxied YARP calls uses a RequestTransform plus Duende's GetUserAccessTokenAsync (because raw token retrieval doesn't handle expiry/refresh), and the Cookie header is stripped with RequestHeaderRemoveTransform.

sources.title: https://timdeschryver.dev/blog/integrating-yarp-within-dotnet-aspire
sources.claim: A YARP BFF gateway in Aspire uses Yarp.ReverseProxy + Microsoft.Extensions.ServiceDiscovery.Yarp with AddServiceDiscoveryDestinationResolver() to avoid hard-coded destinations.

sources.title: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/servers/yarp/direct-forwarding?view=aspnetcore-10.0
sources.claim: IHttpForwarder/MapForwarder provide direct forwarding without YARP's routing, load balancing or config discovery — the minimal proxy primitive.

sources.title: https://github.com/damienbod/bff-aspnetcore-oidc-vuejs
sources.claim: damienbod's BFF sample uses plain cookie + AddOpenIdConnect (no Duende BFF), serves the SPA from wwwroot in production and uses YARP only in development to front the Vite dev server, with AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken on controllers.

sources.title: https://github.com/dotnet/blazor-samples/blob/main/10.0/BlazorWebAppOidcBffAutoYarpAspire/BlazorWebAppOidc/CookieOidcRefresher.cs
sources.claim: Microsoft's CookieOidcRefresher is 102 lines of hand-written refresh logic with no locking/single-flight, and its header comment links to dotnet/aspnetcore#8175.

sources.title: https://duendesoftware.com/blog/20260429-aspnet-core-cookie-size-limits
sources.claim: SaveTokens plus large claim sets overflow the ~4KB cookie / ~8KB header limits, causing HTTP 431 and silent auth failures; the preferred fix is server-side sessions / a custom ITicketStore, with chunking as a tactical stopgap.

sources.title: https://nestenius.se/net/bff-in-asp-net-core-7-introducing-the-duende-bff-library/
sources.claim: Migrating a hand-rolled BFF to Duende collapses the custom BffController into app.MapBffManagementEndpoints(), the proxying into one line, and removes the custom CSRF middleware.

sources.title: https://github.com/ardalis/BFF
sources.claim: ardalis/BFF is a stale fork of the archived Duende BFF repository, not a maintained alternative.

sources.title: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/release-notes/aspnetcore-10.0?view=aspnetcore-10.0
sources.claim: ASP.NET Core 10 shipped the cookie 401/403 change for API endpoints, authentication/authorization metrics, and WebAuthn passkeys; it announces no BFF, refresh-token or DPoP feature.

sources.title: https://auth0.com/blog/authentication-authorization-enhancements-dotnet-10/
sources.claim: Independent round-up of .NET 10 auth changes confirms passkeys, the cookie 401/403 breaking change and new metrics, and lists no BFF or token-refresh feature.

sources.title: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/59443
sources.claim: The ASP.NET Core .NET 10 roadmap listed OAuth 2 refresh-token support (#8175), passkeys (#53467) and DPoP (#58016) as aspirational; no BFF item appears in the authentication section.

sources.title: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/58016
sources.claim: DPoP support in ASP.NET Core is still open and milestoned .NET 11 Planning; the issue notes the only current options are Duende libraries or writing your own.

sources.title: https://github.com/pomerium/pomerium
sources.claim: Pomerium is an Apache-2.0 identity-and-context-aware reverse proxy (zero-trust gateway), latest v0.32.9 (June 2026).

sources.title: https://github.com/thomseddon/traefik-forward-auth
sources.claim: traefik-forward-auth is an MIT-licensed minimal forward-authentication service for Traefik providing Google/OIDC login; latest tag v2.3.0.

sources.title: https://doc.traefik.io/traefik/reference/routing-configuration/http/middlewares/forwardauth/
sources.claim: Traefik's ForwardAuth middleware only delegates authentication to an external service; Traefik OSS does not perform OIDC login itself (its OIDC middleware is a Hub/Enterprise feature).

sources.title: https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_auth_request_module.html
sources.claim: nginx's auth_request module authorizes based on a subrequest result and does not implement OIDC itself.

sources.title: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak-gatekeeper
sources.claim: Keycloak Gatekeeper / louketo-proxy was archived in December 2020 and reached end of life in November 2020.

sources.title: https://github.com/gogatekeeper/gatekeeper
sources.claim: gogatekeeper is the maintained Apache-2.0 community successor to louketo-proxy, latest v4.10.0 (June 2026), supporting Keycloak OIDC discovery.

sources.title: https://docs.duendesoftware.com/bff/fundamentals/session/handlers/
sources.claim: Duende BFF uses the ASP.NET Core OIDC handler, which can be configured against any OpenID Connect provider (IdentityServer, Entra ID, Auth0, Google, Cognito and more) — so Keycloak/OpenIddict work.
